result:
If I had to pick one, I think I'd choose to dramatically increase people's capacity for genuine understanding across differences—the ability to actually grasp how the world looks from perspectives very unlike their own.

I find this compelling because so many other problems seem downstream of its absence. Wars, political dysfunction, cruelty toward outgroups, even failures to address shared challenges like pandemics or climate change—these often persist not because solutions don't exist, but because people can't or won't genuinely model what others experience and value. It's a force multiplier: improve it, and humanity gets better at solving everything else collaboratively.

I'm drawn to this over more direct fixes (ending disease, eliminating poverty) partly because those framings make me uneasy about unintended consequences. A single sweeping change to material conditions, imposed from outside, could go wrong in ways that are hard to predict. Whereas enhancing understanding leaves people's agency intact—they'd still make their own choices, just with better information about each other.

Though I'll admit a counterargument: maybe this is too indirect, and a child dying of malaria today would reasonably prefer the mosquito net over humanity's improved empathy.

What about you? I'm curious whether you'd go for something concrete and material, or something more about how people think and relate to each other.
